h1: The 5 Best Chromebook and Laptop Charging Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Chromebook Charging Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five laptop charging carts from POCHAR, Plugsharge, Pearington and Meteteel, compared by capacity, locks and screen fit.
summary: The POCHAR 30 Unit station is our pick for a mixed Chromebook and laptop fleet. The Plugsharge 32 gives the most capacity, the Pearington 20 suits smaller iPad and Chromebook sets, and the POCHAR 20 and Meteteel 20 cover 20-device rooms.
intro: A charging cart that holds thirty devices is useless if your laptops are 15.6 inches and the slots stop at 14. Screen size, not bay count, is the spec schools get wrong most often.

We reviewed five carts and ranked them on capacity, the largest screen size listed, locking, and how explicitly each listing names Chromebooks. Every cart is in the $200-500 bucket, so the differences come down to fit and features.

products.name: POCHAR 30 Unit Device Charging Station for Chromebook, iPad, 14'' Laptop
products.verdict: 30 numbered bays with a clear Chromebook, iPad and 14 inch laptop claim.
products.description:
The POCHAR 30 Unit station holds 30 devices up to 14 inches and 1.5 inches thick, with numbered bays, four keys and removable doors for cable access. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

The top slot goes to its clear mixed-fleet compatibility wording, which the Meteteel lacks. Against the Plugsharge it holds a couple of fewer devices and a smaller maximum screen.

Good for a classroom mixing Chromebooks, iPads and compact laptops. Not for 15.6 inch machines.
products.idealFor: Classrooms with mixed Chromebooks and tablets.

products.name: Plugsharge 32-Device Laptop Charging Cart for Chromebooks, iPad & Tablets
products.verdict: 32 devices up to 15.6 inches, with surge and ground fault protection.
products.description:
The Plugsharge cart holds 32 devices up to 15.6 inch screens, names Chromebooks explicitly, and lists surge plus ground fault protection and 32 cable organizers. It uses numbered slots and an open rack design.

Second place reflects that an open rack offers less enclosure than a locked cabinet. It beats the POCHAR 30 on capacity and screen size.

Buy it for the largest mixed fleet. Check whether you need a lockable enclosure.

products.name: Pearington 20 Device Mobile Charging and Storage Cart for iPads, Chromebooks
products.verdict: 20 devices, padded bays and locks on both sides.
products.description:
The Pearington 20 has 18 bays plus a shelf for 20-device capacity, fits screens up to 17 inches, and lists padded bays, surge protectors, front and back locks and 2 locking casters.

Third place is because it targets iPads and Chromebooks specifically, giving up capacity versus the 30-plus carts. It does fit larger screens than the POCHAR.

Buy it for a mid-size iPad or Chromebook fleet. Capacity tops out at 20.

products.name: POCHAR 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for iPads Chromebooks, Tablet Charging Station
products.verdict: 20 devices with a 20-outlet surge strip and an anchor chain hook.
products.description:
The POCHAR 20 offers 20-device capacity with explicit iPad and Chromebook compatibility, a 20-outlet power strip with surge protection and a chain hook that anchors the cart.

Fourth place is because it adds little over the Pearington 20 beyond the anchor hook and an outlet strip. It is the smaller sibling of our top pick.

Buy it if you want that anchor point. Maximum screen size is not in our facts.
products.idealFor: Rooms that want a securable 20-device cart.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: 95% pre-assembled with independent front and back locks.
products.description:
The Meteteel cart is 95% pre-assembled, holds 20 devices and has independent front and back locks. It comes in black, in the $200-500 bucket, and its listing does not explicitly name Chromebooks.

It finishes fifth because a missing Chromebook claim makes compatibility harder to confirm than on the POCHAR or Pearington listings. Less assembly time is its trade.

Buy it if setup effort matters most. Verify device fit before ordering.

whatMatters.detail: Each bay has a maximum screen size, such as 14 or 15.6 inches. It matters because a laptop that does not fit will not charge or lock in. Measure your largest device and check the size in the listing.
Capacity is the number of bays, from 20 to 32 here. It matters because you want room for spares. Count your devices and add a few.
Locks stop theft and tampering between classes. It matters in shared rooms. Check whether the cart locks front, back or both.
Surge and ground fault protection protect devices on the shared circuit. It matters when 30 chargers draw at once. Look for it by name.
Some listings name Chromebooks and iPads, others say only laptops. It matters because the vague ones are harder to trust. Prefer explicit wording.

faq.q: Will a 14 inch cart fit my laptops?
faq.a: Only if your devices are 14 inches or smaller. The Plugsharge handles up to 15.6 inches.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Counting bays and ignoring screen size. Check the maximum size first.

faq.q: Is a 30-bay cart worth it over 20?
faq.a: Only if you have the devices. Otherwise the 20-bay carts do the job.
The Meteteel is 95% pre-assembled, while others ship flat-pack or need assembly.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cart?
faq.a: Keep cables tidy and check that locks work. Do not overload the circuit.

faq.q: Does the Meteteel work with Chromebooks?
faq.a: Its listing does not name them, so confirm fit before buying.

finalTake: The POCHAR 30 Unit station is the best all-round cart for mixed fleets. Go to the Plugsharge 32 for larger laptops, and the Pearington 20 for smaller iPad and Chromebook rooms. Always confirm screen size first.
